name: Cafe OTO
note: The fullest experimental programme in London: improv, noise, free jazz, tape music, talks. Own ticketing plus some shows via DICE.

name: IKLECTIK
note: Reborn at Peckham Levels after eviction from Lambeth and two years dark. All ticketing via DICE. Strong autumn programme.

name: New River Studios
note: DIY noise/punk-leaning programme, plus Manorfest in late August. Some shows on WeGotTickets.

name: Servant Jazz Quarters
note: 75-cap basement; mostly songwriter fare with the occasional off-piste gem. Books via DICE.

name: The Waiting Room
note: Basement under the Three Crowns; indie-leaning with occasional occult-synth and electronics nights.

name: The Glove That Fits
note: Tiny room, big bookings. Listings live on Resident Advisor; check Instagram @theglovethatfits.

name: Ormside Projects
note: Arts space in the Penarth Centre with a serious rig and some of the most leftfield club nights in town. Announces late, so check Instagram nearer the time.

name: Venue MOT
note: DIY warehouse club in an old MOT garage on an industrial estate. Rotating promoters, huge system, one of the best dance floors in London. Listings on Resident Advisor.

name: The Carpet Shop
note: Small railway arch on Rye Lane: tacos by day, underground DJs by night, anything from Italo to psytrance. Summer day parties in the courtyard.

name: Hundred Years Gallery
note: Weekend improv sessions in a tiny gallery; listings patchy online, worth checking manually.

name: Union Chapel
note: Mostly mainstream, but the occasional adventurous booking in a spectacular room (Perfume Genius duo, late Oct).

name: Prince Charles Cinema
note: The richest rep programme in London: 35/70mm, all-nighters, Horroctober, director seasons, £1 member screenings.

name: Close-Up Film Centre
note: Rigorous avant-garde and arthouse programming plus a film library and café. Site listings can lag. Check in person.

name: The Garden Cinema
note: Deco-ish independent with constantly rotating seasons: HK Golden Age, Żuławski, queer strands.

name: ICA
note: Exhibitions, radical cinema seasons, and a live programme that quietly books the best experimental acts passing through.

name: BFI Southbank
note: Director and actor seasons, archive rarities, and the London Film Festival in October.

name: Barbican Cinema
note: Curated seasons (kaiju season through October), 35mm events, outdoor summer screenings.

name: The Cinema Museum
note: Film clubs, Kennington Bioscope silents with live piano, and obsessive all-dayers among the projector relics.

name: Genesis Cinema
note: Bar Trash cult nights and premieres with Q&As; listings only appear a few days ahead.

name: Rio Cinema
note: Community-run Dalston landmark, celebrating 50 years through October with 35mm and archival gems.

name: The Castle Cinema
note: Crowdfunded Homerton picture house; classics mixed into the new-release programme.

name: Raven Row
note: Georgian house turned free gallery; always worth the trip regardless of what's on.

name: Auto Italia
note: Artist-run space surfacing radical archives and hosting properly niche evening talks.

name: Studio Voltaire
note: Chapel-turned-gallery with an adventurous performance and off-site programme.

name: Chisenhale Gallery
note: Single-commission programme on a hot streak; in-gallery live events fill up fast.

name: Camden Art Centre
note: Serious exhibitions, good bookshop, garden café. Free.

name: South London Gallery
note: Major free shows plus zine fairs and events across two buildings on Peckham Road.

name: Whitechapel Gallery
note: The thinking person's big institution; one ticket usually covers two major shows.

name: Gasworks
note: First European solos for international artists. The autumn slot is usually the sleeper hit of the season. Free.

name: Goldsmiths CCA
note: Assured programming in a converted Victorian bathhouse. Free.

name: Cell Project Space
note: East London stalwart for emerging and rediscovered practices.

name: Matt's Gallery
note: Legendary artist-led gallery; programme announced in bursts.

name: Toynbee Studios / Artsadmin
note: Live art HQ; autumn London season usually lands in September.

name: London Review Bookshop
note: Basement talks with serious writers; big names sell out fast. Tickets via Eventbrite.
